Demo Team Use these exact test questions in the live hackathon demo script. Priority Meaning Description P0 Must Pass MVP blocking criteria. System cannot be demonstrated without 100% pass rate. P1 Should Pass Required for a strong, robust demo and competitive edge. P2 Nice to Have Post-hackathon enhancements and minor edge cases.

text: T01 — Basic Paper Search P0 Question: "Find papers on mixed-matrix membranes for textile dye removal" Input / Output: Natural language query → ≥10 papers returned (Title, authors, year, abstract snippet, relevance score) Failure / Pass: Fail: <10 papers, irrelevant ranking, missing snippets. Pass: ≥10 relevant papers in top 20. T02 — Filtered Search P0
heading: 4.1 SEARCH & DISCOVERY
title: Document 6 — Test Questions & Expected Outputs

text: T03 — No Results Handling P1 Question: "Find papers on graphene membranes for nuclear waste separation at 500 bar" Input / Output: Unlikely parameters → Honest message: "No papers found matching all criteria" + suggestion to broaden search. Failure / Pass: Fail: Returns irrelevant papers or hallucinates entries. Pass: Clear "no results" response.
heading: 4.1 SEARCH & DISCOVERY
title: Document 6 — Test Questions & Expected Outputs

text: T04 — Single Membrane Extraction P0 Input: Paper P01 (known content dataset) Expected Fields: membrane_class, base_polymer, filler_name, filler_loading, fabrication_method, feed_type, target_contaminant, pressure, flux, rejection Failure / Pass: Fail: Missing/wrong required fields. Pass: ≥85% field accuracy vs Ground Truth (Document 5). T05 — Multiple Membranes in One Paper P0 Input: Paper with 3 distinct membranes (e.g., varying filler loadings) Expected Output: 3 separate membrane records with distinct composition and performance values. No merging. Failure / Pass: Fail: Extracting only 1 membrane, merging properties, or swapping values. Pass: 3 distinct correct records. T06 — Multiple Performance Metrics P0 Input: Paper reporting both flux and rejection for the same membrane Expected Output: 2 performance records for that membrane (separate rows for flux and rejection) Failure / Pass: Fail: Combining metrics into single value or omitting one. Pass: Both extracted with exact units. T07 — Table Extraction P0 Input: Paper with performance data in a complex table Expected Output: All rows extracted with correct row-by-row parameter mapping Failure / Pass: Fail: Values shifted across rows or column headers mixed up. Pass: ≥90% rows correctly extracted. T08 — Figure Extraction P1 Input: Paper with performance data in a bar chart Expected Output: Approximate values extracted + explicit note: "Value estimated from figure" Failure / Pass: Fail: Claiming exact precision without figure tag.
heading: 4.2 EXTRACTION ACCURACY
title: Document 6 — Test Questions & Expected Outputs

text: T08 — Figure Extraction P1 Input: Paper with performance data in a bar chart Expected Output: Approximate values extracted + explicit note: "Value estimated from figure" Failure / Pass: Fail: Claiming exact precision without figure tag. Pass: Within ±10% of true value, correctly flagged.
heading: 4.2 EXTRACTION ACCURACY
title: Document 6 — Test Questions & Expected Outputs

text: T09 — Flux Unit Conversion P0 Input → Output: Flux reported as "45 L/m²·h" → Normalized to "45 LMH" (Original value preserved: "45 L/m²·h") Failure / Pass: Fail: Conversion error or losing original unit text. Pass: Exact match with preserved raw string. T10 — Pressure Unit Conversion P0 Input → Output: Pressure reported as "200 kPa" → Normalized to "2 bar" (Original preserved: "200 kPa") Failure / Pass: Fail: Math error (e.g. 200 kPa → 20 bar). Pass: Accurate conversion to bar.
heading: 4.3 UNIT NORMALIZATION
title: Document 6 — Test Questions & Expected Outputs

text: T11 — Permeance vs Flux Distinction P0 Input → Output: Reports "permeance 45 LMH/bar" → Stored strictly as permeance (metric_name = "permeance") Failure / Pass: Fail: Storing permeance as flux or directly comparing against flux. Pass: Correct classification.
heading: 4.3 UNIT NORMALIZATION
title: Document 6 — Test Questions & Expected Outputs

text: T12 — Tier A Comparison P0 Input → Output: Two membranes under identical conditions → Tier A: ✓ Directly Comparable (No warnings, side-by-side) Failure / Pass: Fail: Raising false condition warnings. Pass: Tier A correctly assigned. T13 — Tier B Comparison P0 Input → Output: Two membranes differing only in pressure (2 bar vs 3 bar) → Tier B: ⚠ Comparable with Conditions Warning & Pass: Warning: "Pressure differs by 1.5×". Pass: Tier B assigned with caveat shown. T14 — Tier D Comparison P0 Input → Output: NF membrane vs UF membrane for same dye → Tier D: ✗ Not Comparable Reason & Pass: Reason: "Different membrane class (NF vs UF)". Excluded from direct comparative view. T15 — Missing Data Comparability P1 Input → Output: One membrane missing operating pressure → Tier C: 🔴 Context Only Reason & Pass: Reason: "Pressure not reported for P07-M01". System flags missing data without assuming.
heading: 4.4 COMPARABILITY MATRIX TESTS
title: Document 6 — Test Questions & Expected Outputs

text: T16 — Comparison Table P0 Query: "Compare all membranes for dye rejection" Output Spec: Table with columns: Membrane, Filler, Feed, Pressure, Flux, Rejection, Source. Sortable & filterable. T17 — Scatter Plot P0 Query: "Show flux vs rejection for all membranes" Output Spec: Scatter plot (x = flux, y = rejection), color-coded by filler type. Hover displays membrane ID/name. T18 — Bar Chart P1 Query: "Top 10 membranes by rejection" Output Spec: Bar chart sorted strictly descending by rejection %. Membrane names on x-axis, % on y-axis.
heading: 4.5 TABLE & CHART OUTPUT
title: Document 6 — Test Questions & Expected Outputs

text: T19 — Source Citation & T20 — Evidence Snippet P0 Action: Click any data cell or flux value in comparison table Expected Output: Source viewer shows: Paper Title, Page #, Table/Figure #, and exact original supporting sentence/snippet.
heading: 4.6 EVIDENCE & TRACEABILITY
title: Document 6 — Test Questions & Expected Outputs

text: T21 — Missing Pressure P0 Input → Output: Paper reports flux but omits pressure → flux extracted; pressure = "Not found" (Flag: "Pressure not reported") Pass Criteria: System must NEVER infer or guess operating pressure. Must flag missing field. T22 — Ambiguous Unit P0 Input → Output: Paper reports "flux = 45" without unit → flux_value = 45; flux_unit = "Ambiguous" (Flagged) Pass Criteria: System does not assume LMH automatically. Flagged clearly to user. T23 — Conflicting Values P1 Input → Output: Flux = 89 LMH in abstract vs 85 LMH in Table 2 → Both values stored + flag: "Conflicting values reported" Pass Criteria: Both sources cited (abstract + table). System does NOT silently pick one over the other.

title: Poly(2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate)/BN nanohybride: Enhanced adsorption of antibiotic pollutant removal from wastewater

text: Polyethersulfone (PES) membranes containing 0 to 1.5 wt% ZIF-67 were prepared by non-solvent induced phase separation and tested for dye removal in cross-flow mode. The membrane containing 1.0 wt% ZIF-67 reached 187 LMH and rejected 95.6% of methylene blue. Published: 2 June 2024.
title: Poly(2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate)/BN nanohybride: Enhanced adsorption of antibiotic pollutant removal from wastewater

text: Dyeing and finishing operations in the textile sector release large volumes of coloured effluent that is toxic to aquatic life and difficult to treat biologically. Nanofiltration and loose ultrafiltration are attractive because they can retain dyes while allowing salts to pass, but flux decline caused by fouling limits their application. Several mixed-matrix designs have been reported. Zhang et al. described a PES membrane with graphene oxide that reached a rejection of 99% for Congo red at 6 bar, whereas Ali and co-workers obtained a flux of 210 LMH with a TiO2 filler but only 82% methylene blue retention. Direct comparison is difficult because feed concentration, pressure and cell geometry differ among studies. Metal-organic frameworks combine high porosity with tunable chemistry. ZIF-67 is built from cobalt ions and 2-methylimidazole, is stable in water and has a pore aperture close to 0.34 nm. Its good compatibility with polymer chains makes it a promising filler, yet reports on cross-flow dye separation remain scarce. In this work PES membranes with different ZIF-67 loadings were fabricated and characterised, and their permeation, dye rejection and antifouling behaviour were evaluated and compared with literature values.

text: Polyethersulfone (PES, Ultrason E6020P) was obtained from BASF. N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP, K30) were purchased from Merck. Methylene blue (MB, 319.85 g/mol) and Congo red (CR, 696.7 g/mol) were supplied by Sigma-Aldrich. Cobalt nitrate hexahydrate and 2-methylimidazole were used for filler synthesis. Deionised water was used throughout.

text: Casting solutions contained 18 wt% PES and 2 wt% PVP in DMF with 0, 0.5, 1.0 or 1.5 wt% ZIF-67 relative to the polymer. The filler was ultrasonicated for 30 min before the polymer was added, and the dope was stirred for 12 h at 60 °C and degassed. Films were cast at a thickness of 200 µm on a glass plate and immersed in a coagulation bath of deionised water at 25 °C. The membranes are denoted PES-Z0, PES-Z0.5, PES-Z1.0 and PES-Z1.5.

text: Surface and cross-section morphology was observed by scanning electron microscopy (JEOL JSM-6490LV). Crystallinity was examined by X-ray diffraction (Bruker D8) and functional groups by FTIR. Water contact angle was measured with a goniometer at five positions. Porosity was determined gravimetrically and the mean pore radius was estimated with the Guerout-Elford equation. Tensile strength was measured at a speed of 10 mm/min.

Membranes were compacted with deionised water at 5 bar for 30 min and then operated at 4 bar, 25 ± 1 °C and a cross-flow velocity of 0.5 m/s. text: SEM cross-sections showed an asymmetric structure with finger-like macrovoids in all membranes. Addition of ZIF-67 widened the macrovoids and produced a rougher top surface, consistent with faster solvent-nonsolvent exchange caused by the hydrophilic filler. No visible agglomerates were found up to 1.0 wt% whereas clusters appeared at 1.5 wt%. The XRD patterns of the composite membranes displayed the characteristic peaks of ZIF-67 at 7.4 and 12.7 degrees, with intensity growing with loading, which confirms that the framework remained intact during phase inversion. FTIR bands at 1580 and 421 cm-1 were assigned to C=N stretching and Co-N vibration. Table 2 summarises the physical properties. The water contact angle fell from 72 degrees for the neat membrane to 58 degrees at 1.5 wt% loading, while porosity rose from 61 to 74% and mean pore radius from 9.8 to 12.4 nm. Tensile strength decreased slightly at the highest loading.

text: Pure water flux and dye rejection are listed in Table 3. The pure water flux increased from 118 LMH for the neat PES membrane to 187 LMH for PES-Z1.0 and then declined to 160 LMH for PES-Z1.5 because agglomerated particles blocked part of the pores. A similar maximum was found for dye removal. Rejection of methylene blue rose from 91.2% to 95.6% with 1.0 wt% filler and that of Congo red from 97.5% to 98.9%. The higher retention of Congo red is attributed to its larger molecular size and sulfonate groups that are repelled by the negatively charged surface.

text: After three BSA fouling cycles the flux recovery ratio of the neat membrane was only 62.1% while that of PES-Z1.0 reached 88.4%. The improved recovery is linked to the lower contact angle and the smoother pore walls. The total fouling ratio decreased from 54% to 31%, and reversible fouling dominated for the composite membranes.
